client_id.description: The rider's own Strava API client ID; empty when the shared application is used.

client_secret_set.description: Whether the rider's own client secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

connected.description: Whether the rider has authorised Wattson at Strava.

connected_at.description: When the rider connected, UTC; null while not connected.

redirect_uri.description: OAuth redirect URI this server sends to Strava: the public URL setting, else the address of this request, plus /api/strava/callback.

scope.description: Comma-separated scopes Strava granted while connected, such as read,activity:write; empty otherwise.

uses_own_app.description: Whether this rider uses their own Strava API application instead of the shared one.

client_id.description: Strava API client ID (digits only); empty when unset.

client_secret_set.description: Whether a Strava client secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned.

client_id.description: Strava API client ID: digits only, at most 12; empty clears it.

client_secret.description: Strava client secret. Omit to keep the stored secret; an empty string clears it.

auto_upload.description: Upload finished rides to Strava automatically.

client_id.description: The rider's own Strava API client ID: digits only, at most 12. An empty string returns the rider to the shared application and removes the own secret. A changed value disconnects the rider.

client_secret.description: The rider's own Strava client secret. Omit to keep the stored secret; a changed value disconnects the rider. Must be sent together with client_id (400 otherwise). Never returned.

activity_id.description: Strava activity ID once done; 0 when there is none.

activity_url.description: Link to the Strava activity once done; empty otherwise.

error.description: Why the last upload failed; empty unless status is error.

status.description: Upload state: none (never uploaded), uploading, done or error.

upload_id.description: Strava upload ID while uploading or done; 0 when there is none.

segments.description: Segments ridden in order, 1 to 100. The total length must not exceed 500 km.

address.description: Bike Bluetooth address to look for, such as AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF. Empty uses the stored address; with none, only the adapter is checked.

host.description: ESPHome proxy as host or host:port. Empty uses the stored host.

key.description: ESPHome API encryption key, base64 of 32 bytes. Empty uses the stored key.

transport.description: local (this host's adapter) or esphome (a Bluetooth proxy). Empty uses the stored setting.

url.description: BRouter base URL to test, such as http://brouter:17777. Empty uses the stored URL.

host.description: ESPHome proxy as host or host:port (default port 6053). Empty uses the stored host.

key.description: ESPHome API encryption key, base64 of 32 bytes. Empty uses the stored key.

token.description: Long-lived access token to test. Empty uses the stored token.

url.description: Home Assistant base URL to test. Empty uses the stored URL.

password.description: Password to test. Empty uses the stored password, but only when the URL is the stored one.

tls_insecure_skip_verify.description: Disable certificate checks for an mqtts:// URL (self-signed broker). WARNING: it lets anyone on the path impersonate the broker. Omit to use the stored setting when the URL is the stored one, otherwise checks stay on.

url.description: MQTT broker URL to test, mqtt:// or mqtts://. Empty uses the stored URL.

username.description: Username to test. Empty uses the stored username, but only when the URL is the stored one.

token.description: Mapillary access token to test. Empty uses the stored token.

latency_ms.description: Time the test took, in milliseconds.

alert.description: Warning for the rider, for example a stale reading; absent when none.

bias.description: Live resistance bias in levels (-10 to 10) added to the route level (route mode) or shifting the interval level (interval mode); 0 in free ride and ERG modes.

block_count.description: Number of blocks in the workout being ridden; 0 outside a workout.

block_index.description: Zero-based index of the current workout block; 0 outside a workout.

block_remaining_s.description: Seconds left in the current workout block; 0 outside a workout.

cadence_rpm.description: Pedalling cadence in revolutions per minute.

connected.description: Whether the link to the bike is up right now.

grade_ahead_pct.description: Road grade at the lookahead point of the route, in percent; 0 when not riding a route.

grade_pct.description: Road grade of the current mode, in percent.

heart_rate_bpm.description: Heart rate in beats per minute; 0 when there is no heart rate source or no reading in the last 5 s.

level.description: Resistance level (1 to 32) the engine last asked the bike for.

mode.description: Ride mode name, for example free.

reported_level.description: Resistance level (1 to 32) the bike last reported; 0 when unknown.

route_id.description: Identifier of the route being ridden; 0 when not riding a route.

route_length_m.description: Length of the route being ridden, in metres; 0 when not riding a route.

speed_kmh.description: Simulated speed in kilometres per hour.

state.description: Ride state: idle, connecting, ready, riding, paused or finished.

target_power_w.description: ERG target power in watts; 0 when the mode has no power target.

workout_id.description: Identifier of the workout being ridden; 0 when not riding a workout.

bytes.description: Bytes on disk (present) or received so far (downloading).

error.description: Why the last download failed, such as HTTP 404.

name.description: Tile name from its south-west corner, such as E5_N45 (5 degrees east, 45 degrees north).

status.description: present: on disk; queued: waiting for its turn; downloading: in progress; error: the last download failed.

total_bytes.description: Size announced by the segments server in bytes; 0 when unknown.

updated_at.description: Last change of the tile's file or download state, UTC.

available.description: Tile names the segments server offers; empty when the index could not be read.

available_error.description: Why the list of available tiles could not be read.

tiles.description: Tiles on disk plus queued, downloading and failed downloads, sorted by name.

last_used_at.description: Last time the token authenticated a request, UTC; null if never. Updated at most once a minute.

prefix.description: First 12 characters of the token, to recognise it.

scopes.description: Scopes the token grants: read, control, admin.

disabled.description: Whether sign-in and every credential of the user is refused.

is_admin.description: Whether the user holds the admin scope.

is_bootstrap.description: Whether this is the first-run admin, who can never be demoted or disabled.

oidc.description: Whether the account is linked to an OIDC identity.

blocks.description: Blocks ridden in order, 1 to 200; the total must not exceed 21600 s (6 h).

type.description: interval sets a resistance level per block; erg holds a target power per block.

duration_s.description: Total length of all blocks in seconds.

owner_id.description: ID of the user who created the workout; 0 when that user has since been deleted.

type.description: interval sets a resistance level per block; erg holds a target power per block.

cookie.description: Session cookie set by the login flow.
cookie.name: wattson_session

info.description: REST API of the Wattson server, which controls a Merach exercise bike. Authenticate with an API token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) or the session cookie set by the login flow. A state-changing request authenticated by the session cookie (this includes routes that document no scope, such as logout) is refused with 403 `csrf` when its Origin header names a foreign host or, with no Origin, the browser reports `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Bearer-token requests are exempt.
info.title: Wattson API

get.description: Returns every configured OIDC provider ordered by display name, enabled or not. Client secrets are never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Adds a provider such as Authentik, Keycloak or any other OpenID Connect server. The slug becomes part of the login and callback URLs and cannot be changed. Register the returned `redirect_uri` at the provider. A duplicate slug returns 409 `slug_taken`. The client secret is sealed at rest and never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

Fetches the discovery document at the URL (the `.well-known/openid-configuration` suffix is added when missing), timing out after 5 seconds, and reports the issuer it publishes. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. Requires the `admin` scope.

delete.description: Removes the provider. Users who signed in through it keep their accounts and sessions, but can no longer sign in with it. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns one provider. The client secret is never returned; `client_secret_set` says whether one is stored. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body. The slug cannot be changed. `client_secret` replaces the stored secret when present; an empty string is rejected with 400, so omit it to keep the current one. A change takes effect on the next sign-in; sessions already open are unaffected. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Verifies a local username and password and sets the session cookie. Attempts are rate limited per remote IP address (the connection's address; X-Forwarded-For counts only when the connection comes from a proxy listed in `auth.trusted_proxies`, and then the rightmost address that is not a trusted proxy is used): after 10 failures in 10 minutes every attempt from that address, whatever the username, returns 429 `rate_limited` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds. Unknown user, wrong password, disabled user and password-less (OIDC) users all return the same 401 `invalid_credentials`. Returns 403 `local_login_disabled` when password sign-in is turned off and the user is not the bootstrap admin. No authentication required.
Deletes the current session, if any, and clears the session cookie. No authentication required.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user, the scopes of the credential in use, and whether it is a session or a token. Requires the `read` scope.

The redirect URI registered at the provider. Checks the provider's `error` parameter, the signed state cookie (same provider, same `state`), exchanges the code with the PKCE verifier, verifies the ID token and its nonce, applies the allowed groups and emails, finds, links or creates the local user, syncs admin status from the admin group, and starts a session. Always answers 302: to the `return_to` path on success, otherwise to `/login?error=<code>` where code is one of `unknown_provider`, `provider_unavailable`, `provider_error`, `state`, `exchange_failed`, `forbidden`, `not_provisioned` or `inactive`. No authentication required.

parameters.description: State echoed by the provider; must match the state cookie.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Error code from the provider, when it refused the sign-in.
parameters.name: error

get.description: Redirects (302) the browser to the provider's authorization endpoint using the authorization code flow with S256 PKCE and a nonce, and sets the short-lived `wattson_oidc` cookie that binds the attempt to this provider. `return_to` must be a same-origin path (it must start with a single `/`); anything else is replaced by `/`. An unknown or disabled provider redirects to `/login?error=unknown_provider`, and one whose discovery fails to `/login?error=provider_unavailable`. No authentication required.

parameters.description: Same-origin path to open after signing in, for example `/settings?tab=bike`. Default `/`.
parameters.name: return_to

post.description: Changes the signed-in user's password. Session only: an API token gets 403 `session_required`. A wrong current password returns 400 `invalid_current_password`. All of the user's sessions are deleted and a fresh session cookie is set. Requires the `read` scope.

get.description: Lists the ways to sign in: whether setup is pending, whether password sign-in is enabled, and the enabled OIDC providers ordered by display name. No authentication required.

Returns the state of the single bike this server controls: idle, connecting, ready, riding, paused or finished, the bound rider, the live protocol and any connection problem with advice to fix it. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Binds one of the caller's riders to the bike (or the simulator) and returns at once with state `connecting`; watch `GET /api/bike` or the WebSocket for `ready` or a connection problem. Any user with control may drive the single bike. Returns 409 `bike_busy` unless the bike is idle, 400 `no_bike_address` when the settings name no bike, and 404 for a rider that is not the caller's. Requires the `control` scope.

Returns the bike to the rider's minimum level and closes the link. Does nothing when idle. Refused with 409 `ride_active` while a ride is riding or paused; use release to end the ride too. Returns 424 `floor_unconfirmed` when the bike was released but not confirmed back at its minimum level. Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes the stored power model of the connected (or, when idle, the configured) bike. A connected bike's model returns to the built-in starting model at once and learns again from the next ride. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns the power model Wattson has learned for the connected bike (or, when idle, for the bike named in the settings): the fitted coefficients, how many ride samples it learned from, whether it is still the built-in starting model, and the modelled watts at 80 rpm for each level. ERG mode uses it to pick the resistance level for a target power. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Ends any ride, returns the bike to the rider's minimum level and closes the link. Idempotent: releasing an idle bike succeeds. Returns 424 `floor_unconfirmed` when the bike was released but could not be confirmed back at its minimum level; the rider must then lower the resistance at the console. Requires the `control` scope.

Scans for Bluetooth devices for `duration_s` seconds (default 5) and lists them, supported bikes first. Empty transport fields use the saved settings. Refused with 409 `bike_busy` while a bike is connected or another scan runs; 424 `scan_failed` when the adapter or proxy cannot be used. Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Checks the host's Bluetooth adapter or the ESPHome Bluetooth proxy that the bike and heart rate monitor use, with the exact fix for each problem found, and lists the configured devices. While a bike is connected the check reuses its live transport; when idle it opens a temporary one and closes it again, and a bike connect or scan arriving meanwhile gets 409 `bike_busy`. It never returns 409 itself: a running scan is reported as code `busy`. With `scan_s` above 0 it scans for that long and reports each device's signal strength (`rssi`), absent when the device was not seen. On a local adapter the scan holds the adapter's scan slot for `scan_s`, which delays the heart rate monitor's search and a bike reconnect meanwhile. It briefly subscribes to an idle ESPHome proxy, which takes the proxy from another client (such as Home Assistant) until it closes. No secret appears in the result. Requires the `admin` scope.

parameters.description: Seconds to scan for the configured bike and heart rate monitor to read their signal strength, 0 to 10. 0 skips the scan.
parameters.name: scan_s

schema.description: Seconds to scan for the configured bike and heart rate monitor to read their signal strength, 0 to 10. 0 skips the scan.

get.description: Lists the number or sensor entities of the saved Home Assistant, sorted by entity id and capped at 1000, for the settings pickers. It always uses the saved URL and token, never ones from the request. Returns 400 `ha_not_configured` without a saved URL and token and 502 `ha_unavailable` when Home Assistant cannot be reached or rejects the token (the message says which). Requires the `admin` scope.

parameters.description: Entity domain to list: number or sensor.
parameters.name: domain

schema.description: Entity domain to list: number or sensor.

parameters.description: Only entities with this device_class attribute, such as power or heart_rate. Empty lists all.
parameters.name: device_class

schema.description: Only entities with this device_class attribute, such as power or heart_rate. Empty lists all.

get.description: Streams the 2048 px JPEG of a Mapillary image through the server, so the browser never talks to Mapillary and never sees the token. `id` is a photo id from `GET /api/routes/{id}/mapillary` (digits only, else 400 `bad_id`; 404 `not_found` for an id no route lists). The response is `image/jpeg` of at most 5 MiB, cacheable by the browser for a day, with the photographer's Mapillary username in `X-Photo-Creator` (percent-encoded when not plain ASCII). Any upstream failure is 502 `photo_unavailable`; 503 `mapillary_unavailable` when the server has no photo support. Requires the `read` scope.

Returns the segments directory state, the tiles on disk and in the download queue, and the tiles the segments server offers (cached for 24 hours; `available_error` explains an unreadable index). Routing needs the tiles a route crosses; each covers 5 by 5 degrees. 409 `no_local_regions` when the segments directory setting is empty. Requires the `admin` scope.

delete.description: Cancels the tile's download if one is running and deletes the tile and any partial file from the segments directory. Succeeds when the tile is not there. 400 `bad_tile_name` for an invalid name; 409 `no_local_regions` when the segments directory setting is empty. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Queues the tile for download from the segments server; tiles download one at a time. A tile already on disk or queued is returned as it is. Poll the list for progress. Errors: 400 `bad_tile_name`; 409 `segments_dir_unavailable` (the directory is missing or not writable) or `no_local_regions` (the segments directory setting is empty). Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Reports whether an MQTT broker URL is configured, whether the bridge is connected to the broker right now, and the latest connection problem (an unreachable broker or a refused login). The bridge keeps retrying by itself; saving the `mqtt` settings reconnects it at once. Requires the `admin` scope.
Returns the latest ride snapshot: state, speed, power, cadence, distance and resistance level. In state `idle` when no bike is connected. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Starts, pauses, resumes or stops the ride, or changes the resistance level. Any user with control may drive the single bike. `start` with `route_id` rides that route with the rider bound to the bike; the ride ends by itself at the route's end. `start` with `workout_id` rides that interval or ERG workout, resolved for the bound rider when the ride starts (editing it later does not change this ride); the ride ends by itself after the last block. `start` with `target_power_w` rides free ERG at that power until stopped; `set_target_power` (value in watts) changes it. `start` takes at most one of `route_id`, `workout_id` and `target_power_w`, and these fields with any other command are a 400 `invalid_request`. Returns 404 `route_not_found` or `workout_not_found` for an unknown route or workout, 400 `invalid_value` for a target power outside 50 to 1000 W, 409 `no_bike` when no bike is connected and 409 `bad_state` when the command does not fit the ride state (for example resume while not paused). Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns the caller's riders, ordered by ID. A user with no rider gets a default one (named after their display name or username) created on the first call. An admin may pass `all=true` to list every user's riders; other users get 403. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.description: Admin only: list the riders of every user instead of only your own.
parameters.name: all

schema.description: Admin only: list the riders of every user instead of only your own.

post.description: Creates a rider owned by the caller. Omitted fields take their documented defaults. Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes one of the caller's riders. The last remaining rider cannot be deleted (409 `last_rider`), nor can the rider bound to the connected bike (409 `rider_in_use`; disconnect the bike first). A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns one of the caller's riders. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `read` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body of one of the caller's riders. The merged profile is validated (`min_level` must not exceed `max_level`). A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Changing the rider bound to the connected bike is allowed, but the connection keeps the profile it was made with: the change applies at the next connect. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns whether the rider can and does use Strava, the rider's own app settings and the redirect URI to register at Strava. No secret or token is returned. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `read` scope.

patch.description: Sets the rider's own Strava API application (`client_id`, `client_secret`) and the `auto_upload` flag; omitted fields are unchanged. Changing the client ID or secret disconnects the rider, because tokens belong to the old application. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Redirects (302) the browser to Strava's authorization page for one of the caller's riders, using the rider's own Strava application or the shared one, and the scopes `read` and `activity:write`. The signed state is bound to the caller and the rider and valid for 10 minutes. `return_to` must be a same-origin path (default `/riders`). Without configured credentials the redirect goes to `<return_to>?strava=error&reason=not_configured` instead. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

parameters.description: Same-origin path to open when the flow ends, for example `/riders`. Default `/riders`.
parameters.name: return_to

get.summary: Start connecting a rider to Strava

post.description: Revokes Wattson's access at Strava (best effort: a Strava failure does not stop it) and forgets the athlete and tokens. The rider's own app credentials and `auto_upload` stay. A rider owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns finished rides of the caller's riders, newest first, without samples. Page by passing the previous page's `next_before` as `before`. With `rider_id` only that rider's rides are listed; a rider of another user returns 404 unless the caller is an admin. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.description: Only this rider's rides. A rider of another user is a 404 unless you are an admin. Default: every ride of your own riders.
parameters.name: rider_id

schema.description: Only this rider's rides. A rider of another user is a 404 unless you are an admin. Default: every ride of your own riders.

parameters.description: Only rides with an ID below this one; pass the previous page's next_before. 0 starts at the newest.
parameters.name: before

schema.description: Only rides with an ID below this one; pass the previous page's next_before. 0 starts at the newest.

delete.description: Deletes a finished ride and its samples. A Strava activity already created from it is not touched. A ride of another user returns 404 unless the caller is an admin; a ride still recording is 409 `ride_in_progress`. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns one finished ride with its samples thinned to at most `points` points (default 600) by averaging. A ride of another user returns 404 unless the caller is an admin; a ride still recording is 409 `ride_in_progress`. Requires the `read` scope.

parameters.description: Most points in the series, 50 to 3600. A longer ride is thinned by averaging.
parameters.name: points

schema.description: Most points in the series, 50 to 3600. A longer ride is thinned by averaging.

get.description: Returns the ride as a FIT activity file (`application/vnd.ant.fit`) with a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header. It does not depend on Strava. A ride of another user returns 404 unless the caller is an admin; a ride still recording is 409 `ride_in_progress`. Requires the `read` scope.

200.description: The ride as a FIT activity file.

get.description: Returns the ride's Strava upload state: `none`, `uploading`, `done` (with the activity) or `error` (with the reason). A ride of another user returns 404 unless the caller is an admin; a ride still recording is 409 `ride_in_progress`. Requires the `read` scope.
get.summary: Get a ride's Strava upload status

post.description: Uploads the ride to its rider's connected Strava account as a FIT activity. The upload runs in the background: the response is 202 with status `uploading` while a worker runs (poll `GET /api/rides/{id}/strava`), and 200 when the ride is already `done`, which is never uploaded again. Only one upload is ever started per ride, however many requests arrive; a failed ride (`error`) can be retried. Strava reporting a duplicate counts as done with the existing activity. Errors: 409 `strava_not_connected` (the rider has not connected Strava), 409 `ride_in_progress`; 503 `shutting_down` while the server stops; 404 for a ride of another user unless the caller is an admin. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns every route, newest first, without geometry. Routes are shared: every signed-in user sees all of them. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Routes between 2 to 30 waypoints with BRouter and, unless `dry_run` is set, stores the result as a route owned by the caller (201, source `draw`, the profile and waypoints kept in `spec`). With `dry_run` nothing is stored and the response is 200 with route id 0. When a local segments directory exists and lacks map regions the line crosses, the request is refused with 422 `missing_tiles` and the tile names in `error.details.missing_tiles` (download them under Map regions), unless the admin enabled the public BRouter fallback in Settings, in which case the waypoints are sent to that public server instead. Other errors: 400 for coordinates out of range; 422 `route_too_short`, `route_too_long` or `no_elevation`; 502 `brouter_unavailable` (BRouter cannot be reached), `brouter_error` (BRouter refused the route) or `elevation_unavailable`. Requires the `control` scope.

Uploads a GPX, TCX or FIT file (multipart/form-data, field `file`, at most 20 MiB) and stores it as a route owned by the caller. Tracks without elevation, or above 60 degrees latitude, are looked up at OpenTopoData when that is enabled in Settings. Errors: 400 `unsupported_format`, `no_track` or `invalid_file` (the file could not be parsed); 413 `too_large`; 422 `no_elevation` (enable OpenTopoData elevation in Settings → Integrations), `route_too_short` (under 50 m), `route_too_long` (over 500 km) or `too_many_points`; 502 `elevation_unavailable` (the elevation service failed). Requires the `control` scope.

parameters.description: Route name. Defaults to the name stored in the file, else the file name without its extension.
parameters.name: name

schema.description: Route name. Defaults to the name stored in the file, else the file name without its extension.

file.description: The route file: GPX, TCX or FIT, at most 20 MiB. The format is detected from the content, then the file name.

post.description: Creates a route from constant-grade segments ridden in order, for example to train a specific climb. The route starts at 100 m elevation. The total length may not exceed 500 km (422 `route_too_long`). Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes a route. Only the route's owner or an admin may do this (403 `not_owner` otherwise). A route the connected ride is using cannot be deleted (409 `route_in_use`); stop the ride first. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns a route with its bounding box, simplified GeoJSON line and spec. Any signed-in user may read any route. Requires the `read` scope.

patch.description: Changes the route's name. Only the route's owner or an admin may do this; anyone else gets 403 `not_owner`. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns the Mapillary street photos selected along the route: at most one per 15 m, each with its distance along the route and camera heading. The list is built in the background the first time it is asked for (`status` `building`; poll every few seconds), cached for 30 days and rebuilt when the Mapillary token changes. Fetch a photo's image from `GET /api/mapillary/images/{id}`. The token is never returned. Requires the `read` scope.
get.summary: Get the street photos along a route

get.description: Returns the route resampled every `step_m` metres as parallel arrays (latitude, longitude, elevation, grade). The response is gzip-compressed when the client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Requires the `read` scope.

Returns the whole configuration. Secrets are write-only: each is reported as a `*_set` boolean (`bike.esphome_key_set`, `ha.token_set`, `mqtt.password_set`, `mapillary.token_set`, `strava.client_secret_set`) and the value is never returned. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes the fields present in the body and leaves the rest alone. Secret fields are write-only: omit one to keep the stored value, send an empty string to clear it, or send a value to replace it. The merged result is validated as a whole; a bad value returns 400 `invalid_setting` with the message `<section.field>: <problem>` and nothing is stored. Changing any `mapillary` field restarts a street photo build in progress. Changing any `mqtt` field reconnects the MQTT bridge at once. Changing `strava.client_id` or `strava.client_secret` disconnects every rider connected through the shared app (best-effort revoke at Strava); riders with their own app are untouched. Returns the new settings in the same shape as the GET. Requires the `admin` scope.

post.description: Scans for 5 seconds with the local adapter or the ESPHome proxy and looks for the bike's address. Without an address it only reports how many devices were seen. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. Refused with 409 `bike_busy` while a bike is connected, because one adapter cannot scan while holding a bike. Requires the `admin` scope.
post.summary: Test the Bluetooth adapter and bike

post.description: With at least one map region downloaded, asks BRouter for a 500 m route at the centre of that region and reports the routed length. Without any, only checks that something answers HTTP at `{url}/brouter`. Times out after 10 seconds, does not follow redirects and reports no reply text from the server, only status codes. An empty `url` uses the stored one. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Connects to the ESPHome device, performs the encrypted handshake and reads its device info, then disconnects, timing out after 5 seconds. It never subscribes to Bluetooth and never talks to the bike, so it is safe during a ride. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A device without the Bluetooth proxy component reports `no bluetooth_proxy`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Calls `GET {url}/api/` with the token as a bearer credential, timing out after 5 seconds. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A 401 from Home Assistant reports `token rejected (401)`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Makes one small Graph API request with the token as an OAuth credential in a header (never in a URL), timing out after 5 seconds. An empty `token` uses the stored one. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A 401 or 403 reports `token rejected (401)`. The token is never echoed back. Requires the `admin` scope.

Makes one MQTT 5 connection with a random client id, timing out after 5 seconds, and disconnects. It publishes and subscribes to nothing. Empty body fields fall back to the stored settings, but the stored username and password are only used when the URL is the stored one. The result is always HTTP 200; check `ok`. A refused login reports the CONNACK reason, for example `not authorized`. Requires the `admin` scope.

Creates the bootstrap admin, optionally saves the public URL, and signs the new admin in with a session cookie. If saving the public URL fails after the admin was created, the failure is logged and the admin is still created. Fails with 409 `already_setup` once any user exists. No authentication required.

schema.description: Session cookie for the new admin.

get.description: Reports whether first-run setup is still needed. No authentication required.

The redirect URI registered at Strava. Needs the session cookie of the user who started the flow; the signed state must belong to that user. Always answers 302 to the `return_to` path of the state: `?strava=connected` on success, otherwise `?strava=error&reason=<reason>` where reason is one of `denied` (the user refused), `state` (missing, tampered, expired or another user's state, or the rider is gone), `scope` (Strava did not grant `read` and `activity:write`) or `exchange_failed`. Without a session it redirects to `/login`.

parameters.description: State issued by the connect redirect.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: Error code from Strava, such as access_denied.
parameters.name: error

get.summary: Finish connecting a rider to Strava

get.description: Returns the caller's own API tokens, without their secrets. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Creates a token for the signed-in user and returns its plaintext exactly once. Session only: an API token gets 403 `session_required`. The scopes must be held by the caller, otherwise 403 `scope_exceeds`. Requires the `read` scope.

delete.description: Deletes one of the caller's own tokens. Revocation takes effect immediately. A token owned by someone else returns 404. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns every user account, ordered by ID. Requires the `admin` scope.

patch.description: Changes a user's admin or disabled flag. Disabling a user deletes all of that user's sessions. The bootstrap admin cannot be demoted or disabled (409 `bootstrap_protected`), and the last enabled admin cannot be removed (409 `last_admin`). Requires the `admin` scope.

get.description: Returns every workout with its blocks, newest first. Workouts are shared: every signed-in user sees all of them. Requires the `read` scope.

post.description: Creates a workout owned by the caller. Blocks are validated: 1 to 200 blocks of 5 to 7200 s, at most 21600 s in total; interval blocks set exactly one of `level` or `level_offset`, ERG blocks exactly one of `power_w` or `ftp_pct`. A violation is a 400 `invalid_request` whose message names the field, for example `blocks[2].power_w: exactly one of power_w or ftp_pct required for erg`. Requires the `control` scope.

delete.description: Deletes a workout. Only the workout's owner or an admin may do this (403 `not_owner` otherwise). A workout the connected ride is using cannot be deleted (409 `workout_in_use`); stop the ride first. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns a workout with its blocks. Any signed-in user may read any workout. Requires the `read` scope.

put.description: Replaces the workout's name, type and blocks. Only the workout's owner or an admin may do this (403 `not_owner` otherwise). Blocks are resolved when a ride starts, so an edit applies to the next ride only. Validation errors are as for create. Requires the `control` scope.

get.description: Returns 200 while the server is running. No authentication required.

Upgrades to a WebSocket that streams the bike status and ride ticks and accepts ride commands. Offer the `wattson.v1` subprotocol (400 without it); authenticate with the session cookie (the Origin header must name this server or the public URL, else 403) or by also offering the subprotocol `bearer.<token>`. At most 32 connections are open at once, 8 per user (503 beyond that). The message formats are in the AsyncAPI document, docs/asyncapi.yaml. Requires the `read` scope.
